Question: Prove that the square root of 2 is irrational.
reference_answer: Assume sqrt(2) = p/q in lowest terms. Then p^2 = 2q^2, so p^2 is even and p is even. Write p = 2k, giving 4k^2 = 2q^2 and q^2 = 2k^2, so q is also even. This contradicts that p/q is in lowest terms; hence sqrt(2) is irrational.
keywords: irrational number, contradiction, square root, lowest terms

Question: Find the zeroes of the polynomial x^2 - 5x + 6 and verify the relationship between the zeroes and the coefficients.
reference_answer: Factorising, x^2 - 5x + 6 = (x - 2)(x - 3), so zeroes are 2 and 3. Sum = 5 = -(-5)/1 and product = 6 = 6/1, matching -b/a and c/a.
keywords: quadratic polynomial, zeroes, factorisation, sum of zeroes, product of zeroes
